# Rakshith Bangalore

> Rakshith Bangalore (full name Rakshith Bangalore Kumaraswamy) is a robotics engineer based in the United Kingdom and Singapore who architects robot solutions across hardware and software. Rakshith is passionate about getting robots out of the lab and into productive work, was involved in starting a robotics programme at Nottingham Trent University, and learnt most of the craft hands-on: running demos, teleoperating robots, building reinforcement learning pipelines and testing new methods on humanoid robots. Note: "Bangalore" is part of the name; Rakshith is not based in Bangalore, India.

## Positioning
- Robotics engineer who architects solutions: humanoid robots, simulation and sim-to-real, robot hardware and software.
- Focus: getting humanoids, quadrupeds and AMRs into productive use cases that run round the clock.
- Open to speaking at events, conferences and panels, podcasts, and collaborations in robotics.
- Talks with businesses about where humanoids, quadrupeds and AMRs fit their work, and invites early adopters of humanoid robots. No obligation.
- Organisations worked with: Nottingham Trent University, PepsiCo, Unitree, Autodiscovery, Fragrance Castle.

## Facts
- Humanoid robotics: two years of industrial use cases on Unitree H1-2 and G1 humanoid robots for a PepsiCo programme; neural policies for legged control, sim-to-real transfer, actuator identification.
- Fragrance Castle (2026, Kyne Robotics case study): two AgiBot G2 humanoids (one with Shadow five-finger hands, one with a suction tool) and an AMR run a perfume warehouse, online-order packing line and luxury boutique in Isaac Sim 6.0.1; site designed to Singapore building rules; 120 s film in which all 16 shots passed a per-frame collision and motion check; 314 automated tests. Simulation only.
- WardZero (2026): open platform to develop and test hospital robots in simulation; simulated hospital with a surgical wing, Isaac Sim and MuJoCo, a safety layer with seven modes, ROS 2 navigation (99.6% map wall accuracy); reference robot Unitree G1 with BrainCo Revo2 hands. Simulation only so far.
- Industry 4.0 mobile manipulator (award-winning MEng capstone): UR-10 arm on an Omron LD250 mobile base with a SmartShift tool changer, scoped with Walkers around a live factory workflow.
- Laparoscopic surgery trainer: project manager of an eight-person team with an NHS Trust; compliant force-feedback mechanism.
- Aircraft cabin lab: decommissioned Embraer ERJ 145 converted into a flight-comfort research laboratory for EU Clean Sky 2 (Comfdemo).
- Product delivery: an AI-enabled full-stack post-production software platform (pilot post-production reduced from 4 days to 4 hours) and a portable podcasting solution moving to its first production run.
- Education: MEng, Nottingham Trent University.
